newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities tumble after data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond volatilities tumble after data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options tumbled as the bond market rallied on a moderate reading in the January U.S. employment report, dealers said.
"As you can expect, they opened up higher before the number," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT). "After the number, they got hit incredibly hard."

Implied volatility for CBOT March T-bond futures options plummeted to 9.5 percent -- even when calculated on Monday's date, discounting the weekend decay -- after opening at 10.5 against Thursday's 10.3 closing.

Based on today's date, the same premium levels would imply March volatility to be below nine percent, but traders said market makers in the pit had started using Monday's date soon after the jobs data, pricing out the weekend decay.

Non-farm payrolls increased by 271,000 in January, against a revised 261,000 gain in December, well above average Wall Street estimates of 237,000. But traders said the estimates had ranged very widely, up to more than 400,000, and the January number was perceived to be market-friendly.
A rise in the jobless rate to 5.4 percent in January from December's 5.3 percent was also seen to be positive.
March T-bond futures rallied on the data by more than a full point to a high of 113-00 before pulling back slightly.
Some firms that had bought huge amounts of March 109 and 110 puts earlier in the week were said to be getting out of those positions as those short-dated options were hit by severe time decay.
An investment bank that bought 12,000 contracts of March 109 puts on Thursday was seen selling some 6,000 of them back early in the morning.
Traders expect volatilities to meander in lower ranges next week.

They noted that although the Treasury's refunding could weigh on bond prices, and although retail sales and producer price data were coming out next week, fears of a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike had dissipated after this week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and employment data.
In addition, next Friday is a half-day ahead of a long weekend due to the Presidents Day holiday on Monday, February 17.
With the CBOT March options expiring on February 21 and trading yet to pick up in April or June contracts, traders said activity was likely to be subdued for a while.
The shorter end of the yield curve also saw volatilities fall from their already depressed levels.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options fell by nearly a full point each to 9.8 and 13.0 percent respectively.

"They hit the fronts hard, but even the reds (March 1998 to December 1998 contracts) are down quite a bit," said an investment bank trader, noting that March 1998 volatility was off half a point to about 15.3 percent.
"I think dealers were heavy sellers probably for about the first hour of the day," he added. "Volume is pretty good."
